title: Why Procurement?
purpose: Show that Procurement creates different kinds of value depending on business context.

requests.context: Approved catalog item; preferred supplier; negotiated unit price €1,050.
requests.procurement_value: Use existing commercial path; avoid unnecessary sourcing.

requests.context: Production-critical timing; existing supplier and inbound supply must be investigated.
requests.procurement_value: Protect continuity through evidence, supplier confirmation and exception handling.

requests.context: Vague scope, multiple capable suppliers, subjective/technical evaluation needed.
requests.procurement_value: Clarify requirement, create competitive process, normalize proposals and govern award.

requests.context: Production line down; approved emergency contractor available; delay costs far exceed sourcing benefit.
requests.procurement_value: Protect continuity while documenting exception and commercial reasonableness.

requests.context: Engineering suggests one supplier; prototype capability, IP and technical iteration matter more than simple unit price.
requests.procurement_value: Test capability, risk, commercial terms and single-source justification without forcing fake competition.

anti_patterns: Only spend above a fixed threshold deserves Procurement.
Procurement value is always the lowest price.
Every requirement should be competed even when an emergency or justified single-source case makes that irrational.
strong_principle: Procurement chooses the lightest process that still protects value, continuity, competition, risk and governance for the specific need.
